instruction:
You have been tasked with designing a simple CPU using Verilog. One of the required components of the CPU is an Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) that performs various arithmetic and logical operations on two 32-bit inputs. You are required to design the ALU module that takes in two 32-bit inputs, a 5-bit control signal, and outputs the result of the operation.

The ALU should support the following operations:

- Addition (signed and unsigned)
- Subtraction (signed and unsigned)
- Bitwise AND
- Bitwise OR
- Bitwise XOR
- Bitwise NOR
- Set Less Than (signed and unsigned)
- Shift Left Logical
- Shift Right Logical
- Shift Right Arithmetic
- Load Upper Immediate

The control signal (aluc) is a 5-bit input that determines which operation the ALU should perform. The table below shows the mapping between the control signal and the corresponding operation:

| aluc | Operation |
|------|-----------|
| 00000| Addition (signed) |
| 00001| Addition (unsigned) |
| 00010| Subtraction (signed) |
| 00011| Subtraction (unsigned) |
| 00100| Bitwise AND |
| 00101| Bitwise OR |
| 00110| Bitwise XOR |
| 00111| Bitwise NOR |
| 01000| Set Less Than (signed) |
| 01001| Set Less Than (unsigned) |
| 01010| Shift Left Logical |
| 01011| Shift Right Logical |
| 01100| Shift Right Arithmetic |
| 01110| Load Upper Immediate |
| 11111| Zero (output 0) |

You are required to implement the ALU module using Verilog. Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs:
- a (32-bit input)
- b (32-bit input)
- aluc (5-bit input)

Outputs:
- result (32-bit output)

Your module should be self-contained and should not rely on any external modules. Your Verilog code should be within 200 lines.
